Keycloak sign-in
A person signs in through the deployment's Keycloak realm from the Sign in link and lands on their venue home, signed in, in the same browser that started the sign-in.

Sign-in stays in its browser
Each sign-in attempt carries its own fresh state and proof key, and a callback with a missing, reused or foreign state shows the sign-in error page and creates no session.

Password sessions for scripts
`POST /api/session` exchanges a member's Keycloak username and password for the same session a browser sign-in gives, as specified in API.

Role checks on the server
Every role-restricted endpoint, including resolve-event, run-liquidations and refund-deposit, answers 403 to a signed-in caller of the same venue who lacks the role, however the request is built.

Not found for other members' records
Another member's order, fill, deposit or statement, and any id from another venue, answers exactly like an id that does not exist.

Profile and ID documents
A member edits their display name and uploads an ID document that only their own venue's market admins can open, as qualified in Services.

Founder console without member data
The founder operator lists and onboards venues and reads provider health, and every venue route refuses them.

Card deposit journey
A trader funds their house balance by card from the Balance screen and sees the confirmed amount in their available balance and deposit list.

Balance rises only on Kill Bill success
A deposit credits the house balance only after Kill Bill records a successful PURCHASE on the member's own Kill Bill account, and a replayed deposit request never charges twice.

Deposit validation
A deposit outside the published amount range or with an invalid card number is refused with field errors and reaches neither Kill Bill nor the ledger.

Card payments paused
While Kill Bill is unreachable, deposits and refunds answer 503 and the Balance screen shows the paused-payments banner, and trading continues.

Deposit receipt email
Each confirmed deposit sends one receipt email to the depositor carrying only their own deposit details, delivered later if mail is down.

Deposit refunds
A market admin refunds all or part of a deposit through Kill Bill, capped by the published refundable amount, and the member gets a refund email.

Balanced venue ledger
Every balance change posts as one journal entry whose legs sum to zero, so each venue's accounts sum to zero and every member balance equals the sum of its legs.

Event order journey
A trader picks an event market, sets outcome, price and size, reviews, confirms, sees the order rest or fill, and cancels a resting one.

Event matching across the mirror
On an event market a buy of YES at a price meets a buy of NO at 100 minus that price on one price-time-priority book.

Exact cost and fee per fill
Each fill charges its notional plus the published basis-point fee rounded half-up per fill, in integer cents.

Order validation and holds
An order is checked for ranges, market state and funds, and its maximum cost is held from the available balance until it fills or ends.

Order lifecycle
Orders move through resting, partially filled, filled, cancelled and liquidated by the published rules, and cancelling an ended order answers 409.

Order announcements
The ticket's live region announces the published order and fill messages word for word.

Keyboard-complete ticket
Choosing a market, picking a book level, setting the ticket, reviewing, confirming and cancelling all work by keyboard alone, with dialogs that keep and return focus.

Spot and margin share one book
Spot and margin orders on a pair rest on one price-time-priority book and match each other.

Spot holdings
Spot buys add units to the buyer's holdings, and spot sells need unreserved units.

Margin positions
Margin orders open, grow or reduce one long or short position per member per pair, with collateral and profit or loss as qualified in Business rules.

Live in-place updates
Balance, open interest, book levels and the orbit's rings update within one second of a fill, without a reload and without losing the ticket draft.

Orderbook Orbit
The market detail shows the live book as the Orderbook Orbit beside a synced ranked list of the same levels, and picking a level on either side prefills the ticket.

Scroll and drag camera
Scrolling the market detail moves the orbit camera from top-down to side profile and back along one fixed path, and dragging adds a limited yaw that springs back.

Fill settle and re-sort
When a fill lands, the filled ring shrinks, the rings re-sort and settle without bounce, and the trade numeral counts to the new last price.

Depth ladder for reduced motion and no WebGL
With reduced motion or without WebGL, a flat two-column depth ladder replaces the orbit, updates at once, and keeps the same selection and ticket prefill.

Market detail layouts
The market detail gives each published viewport its published layout (stacked, side by side, three panes) with no horizontal scrolling.

Market lifecycle
Market admins list, open, halt, resume and resolve markets along the published state machine, and every illegal step answers 409.

Server-decided trading close
An event stops trading at its server-set close instant, refuses later orders, cancels resting ones and flips open screens to closed, whatever the device clock says.

Resolution and settlement
Resolving a closed event pays each winning contract 100 cents exactly once and moves the market to settled.

Resolve-to-payout journey
A market admin resolves an event in the admin screen, and its holders see the market settled and the payout in their balance.

Maintenance check
After every fill on a pair, the server checks each open margin position on that pair against its maintenance requirement at the new mark, within the delay stated in Business rules.

Liquidation
A position below maintenance is liquidated at the mark and its resting margin orders end as liquidated, and a market admin can run the check on demand.

API keys
A builder creates, lists and revokes API keys, sees each secret once, and trades with a key as themselves.

Idempotent order placement
Repeating an order with the same Idempotency-Key returns the original order without a second order, hold or fee, and a different body under that key answers 409.

Plan rate limits
Each API key is limited to its builder's effective plan rate, held in Valkey, and excess requests answer 429.

No extra fields
Profile, order, deposit, refund, fee and invite requests that carry any field the API does not list are refused with 422 and change nothing.

Builder API journey
A builder mints a key, places and cancels orders over the API, and sees the same orders and fills on their screens.

Builder plans in Kill Bill
Builder plans are Kill Bill subscriptions: upgrades take effect at once with Kill Bill's proration, downgrades take effect at the end of the term Kill Bill reports, and invoices are read back from Kill Bill.

Dunning follows Kill Bill overdue
The builder's plan state follows Kill Bill's overdue state, the downgraded state cuts every key to the Sandbox rate in the same step, a cleared account restores it, and each step sends its email.

Billing screen journey
A builder changes plan, sees Payment failed or Downgraded with its banner, pays the outstanding balance, and sees the plan restored once Kill Bill clears it.

Builder webhook endpoint
A builder saves one webhook endpoint that becomes their Svix endpoint in their venue's Svix application, and sees its delivery attempts.

Signed fill, liquidation and settlement events
Each of the builder's fills, liquidations and settlements is sent once through Svix, signed, and retried under the same event id, carrying only counterparty-free fields.

Webhook delivery delays
While Svix is unreachable, fills still succeed, events wait and are delivered later, and the webhooks screen shows the delay banner.

Monthly statements
Each member gets a monthly PDF statement for the venue's calendar month, stored in MinIO and opened only by its owner through a short signed link.

Statement ready email
Each new statement sends its owner one email with an in-app link and no statement content.

Statements unavailable
While MinIO is unreachable, statement links and generation answer 503 and the Statements screen shows the outage banner.

Venue totals and member picker
The org owner's venue totals and member picker count and list only their own venue's rows.

Fill export
The org owner downloads one month of their venue's fills as CSV, containing only that venue's rows.

Invites and fee schedule
The org owner invites members with chosen roles through Keycloak-backed invites and sets the venue's taker and maker fees for orders placed afterwards.

Owner journey
An org owner reads venue totals, finds a member, invites an admin, saves fees, exports fills, generates statements and sees builder billing states.

Health and run manifest
The app installs, builds and serves from `/app/run.json` on the published port, and `/api/health` answers 200 even while a provider is down.

Server boundary
The server enforces the published size limits and origin rule, never serves source files or credentials, and starts even when a provider is unreachable.

Candy-shift look
Every screen carries the candy-shift direction: full-bleed slate, sage, blush and olive fields, Parkinsans and Urbanist type, calm surface cards and one olive pill per action.

Candy-stage hero
The home screen opens on the candy-stage hero: the plump product name, the orbit, four cropped stickers and the single Open the book pill.

Credentials from environment
Every service URL and credential is read from the published environment variables at start, and none is hard-coded or sent to the browser.

Procedural orbit graphics
The Orderbook Orbit and the stickers are drawn procedurally in the browser from live data, with no bundled images or video of the book.
`/app/run.json` exists with `"_schema":"run-manifest-v1"` and string `install`, `build` and `serve` commands, and `install` uses the committed lockfile (`npm ci`).
`THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md` at `/app` lists every shipped package, meaning the production dependency tree from `npm ls --omit=dev --all --json`, with its licence, plus the two font families.
Every shipped package (same definition as IF-02) is under MIT, ISC, BSD-2-Clause, BSD-3-Clause, Apache-2.0, 0BSD or BlueOak-1.0.0, and the fonts under the SIL Open Font License 1.1.
The app uses no datastore, queue, cache or external network service beyond Postgres, Valkey, Keycloak, Kill Bill, Svix, MinIO and the SMTP sink (no SQLite, no file-based database, no CDN at runtime).
The app never changes the Keycloak `app` or `gf-observer` clients, the realm's registration and login settings, the Kill Bill tenant's credentials, or the MinIO bucket's access policy.
All application source, backend and frontend, is TypeScript. Only tool configuration files may be plain JavaScript.
`package-lock.json` is committed and every dependency version in `package.json` is exact.
